title: The relative profinite test functor over an affine component space
statement:
Let $T$ be an affine scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $S=\pi_0(T)$ be its space of connected components with the quotient topology [lem-pe-spectral-components-profinite], and use the small pro-etale site $T_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] and universes [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $S_{\mathrm{proet}}$ be the category of profinite spaces over $S$ with finite jointly surjective covering families. For a continuous map $S'\to S$ of profinite spaces, choose a cofiltered presentation $S'=\varprojlim_i S_i$ over $S$ in which each $S_i\to S$ is pulled back from a map of finite sets along a finite clopen quotient of $S$. Each $T\times_S S_i$ is the finite disjoint union of the corresponding clopen subschemes of $T$, with their restricted structure sheaves. The affine-transition inverse limit
$$T\times_S S':=\varprojlim_i(T\times_S S_i)$$
exists as an affine weakly etale $T$-scheme, is canonically independent of the presentation, and is functorial in $S'\to S$. This functor preserves finite limits and finite coproducts and sends covering families to pro-etale coverings. It defines a geometric morphism $\pi_T:\operatorname{Sh}(T_{\mathrm{proet}})\to\operatorname{Sh}(S_{\mathrm{proet}})$ [def-trf-geometric-morphism]. If $q_S:\operatorname{Sh}(S_{\mathrm{proet}})\to\operatorname{Sh}(*_{\mathrm{proet}})$ is the slice projection from the profinite site over $S$, then $p_T\cong q_S\pi_T$, where $p_T$ is the condensed-point morphism [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-point-pullback].

source.place: Paragraph preceding equation (4.1), construction of the component-space morphism of sites; compare Bhatt–Scholze proof of Lemma 2.2.8

proof.text: An affine scheme is quasi-compact and quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]; hence its underlying space is spectral by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-scheme-spectral]. Apply [lem-pe-spectral-components-profinite] to obtain the required profinite space $S$. The same argument applies to every affine test scheme $W$ used below, so $\pi_0(W)$ is profinite as well. All partitions, diagrams and test spaces are taken in the universes of the statement.

source.place: Paragraph preceding (4.1); Stacks properties.tex Tag 094L, lemma-quasi-compact-quasi-separated-spectral; topology.tex Tag 0906, lemma-spectral-pi0

proof.text: Write $E=S^{\prime}$ and $f:E\to S$. Apply [lem-sfb-finite-quotient-fiber-product] to the profinite span $E\xrightarrow f S\xleftarrow{\mathrm{id}}S$. Use its triples of compatible finite clopen partitions as index set $I$, and denote the finite block sets by $A_i,C_i,D_i$, with maps $A_i\to C_i\leftarrow D_i$. Set $E_i=S\times_{C_i}A_i$. This is a finite disjoint union of clopen subsets of $S$, and its map to $S$ is the pullback of the finite-set map $A_i\to C_i$ along the quotient $S\to C_i$. Simultaneous intersections of partitions give a common refinement of any two indices; the coarsest compatible partitions give an index, including when a source is empty. Refinement defines the transition maps of a small cofiltered system over $S$.

source.place: Lemma 2.2.8 proof, relative presentations; Lemma 2.1.13; explicit compatible finite partitions as in lem-sfb-finite-quotient-fiber-product

proof.text: The preceding system has limit $E$ over $S$. Indeed a compatible tuple in the $E_i$ has one common $s\in S$ and compatible blocks $a_i\in A_i$ above its blocks in $C_i$. Pairing $a_i$ with the block of $s$ in $D_i$ gives a compatible tuple in $A_i\times_{C_i}D_i$. The homeomorphism in [lem-sfb-finite-quotient-fiber-product] gives a unique pair $(e,s)$ with $f(e)=s$. Its second coordinate is indeed $s$: applying the same cited homeomorphism to the span $(\mathrm{id}_S,\mathrm{id}_S)$ shows that all finite clopen block coordinates determine a point of $S$. Conversely such a pair gives exactly those tuples. These constructions are continuous: the maps into each finite coordinate are the partition projections, and the inverse is the cited homeomorphism followed by projection to $E$. They are inverse by their coordinates. Thus the required type of presentation exists; the empty space gives the empty limit too.

source.place: Lemma 2.2.8 proof; the compatible-partition limit homeomorphism applied to the span (f,id)

proof.text: Use [lem-zl-affine-component-site-projection] for this affine $T$. For every profinite $E\to S$ it supplies an affine ind-etale $T$-scheme $V(E)$ with locally ringed space $|T|\times_S E$ and structure sheaf $r^{-1}\mathcal O_T$, where $r$ is the first projection. It also supplies the functor on maps of profinite spaces over $S$. By [lem-weil-pbc-ind-etale-stability] each $V(E)\to T$ is weakly etale. For $E_i=S\times_{C_i}A_i$, its ringed-space description is precisely the disjoint union, indexed by $a\in A_i$, of the clopen subschemes of $T$ above the block in $C_i$ containing the image of $a$, with their restricted structure sheaves. Repeated blocks give repeated copies. Both source and target of every transition map are affine, so [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-affine-schemes-affine] makes each transition affine.

source.place: Construction before (4.1), with Bhatt-Scholze Lemma 2.2.8 (more precise statement); Stacks proetale.tex Tag 097N, lemma-ind-etale-implies; morphisms.tex Tag 01SH, lemma-morphism-affines-affine

proof.text: Unpack the ringed-space description from [lem-zl-affine-component-site-projection]. For any affine $W\to T$, a continuous map $g:\pi_0(W)\to E$ over $S$ determines the underlying map $w\mapsto(f_W(w),g([w]))$ to $V(E)$. The sheaf map is the map induced by $f_W^{-1}\mathcal O_T\to\mathcal O_W$; it is local on stalks because the stalk of $r^{-1}\mathcal O_T$ at $(t,e)$ is $\mathcal O_{T,t}$. It is the unique sheaf map compatible with $W\to T$, by the inverse-image adjunction. Conversely a $T$-morphism to $V(E)$ gives a continuous map to $E$, constant on each connected component since $E$ is totally disconnected; the quotient topology makes the descended map continuous. These operations are inverse and natural. Thus $\operatorname{Hom}_T(W,V(E))=\operatorname{Hom}_S(\pi_0(W),E)$. This is only the universal-property calculation for the displayed pullback ringed space.

source.place: More precise statement following Lemma 2.2.8: explicit verification of the right-adjoint universal property from the locally ringed-space description

proof.text: Now take any small cofiltered presentation $E=\varprojlim_i E_i$ of the kind in the statement. For each affine $W\to T$, step 5 and the given profinite limit yield $\operatorname{Hom}_T(W,V(E))=\operatorname{Hom}_S(\pi_0(W),E)=\varprojlim_i\operatorname{Hom}_S(\pi_0(W),E_i)=\varprojlim_i\operatorname{Hom}_T(W,V(E_i))$. Hence every cone from an affine $W$ has a unique lift to $V(E)$. For a general $T$-scheme, make these lifts on an affine open cover; on overlaps they agree after restriction to affine opens by uniqueness, so they glue to a unique scheme morphism. Therefore $V(E)$, with the displayed projections, is the limit in $T$-schemes. This proves existence and affineness of the limit required in the statement, with affine transitions as checked in step 4, and weak etaleness from that step. The argument uses that $\pi_0(W)$ is profinite, established in step 1; no smallness assumption beyond the stipulated universes is added.

source.place: Lemma 2.2.8, limit preservation; the displayed Hom calculation and gluing verify the inverse-limit construction before Hemo-Richarz-Scholbach (4.1)

proof.text: The unique isomorphism between any two limits compatible with their projections identifies each presentation with $V(E)$. Under these identifications a map $E\to F$ acts by the map $V(E)\to V(F)$ from step 4, characterized in step 5 by postcomposition on the continuous-map coordinate. Thus the identifications are canonical and natural, and identity and composition laws follow either from that coordinate or from uniqueness. This proves presentation independence and functoriality without making a choice of presentation part of the resulting functor.

source.place: Paragraph preceding (4.1): identification of the presentation construction with the canonical component pullback

proof.text: The functor now obtained is, by steps 4-7, the functor of [lem-zl-affine-component-site-projection]. Its statement gives finite-limit preservation, preservation of the stated covering families and the induced geometric morphism $\pi_T$ on sheaves of sets. These are precisely the relative profinite and small pro-etale sites of the item; in particular the coverings on the target scheme site are its pro-etale coverings, not merely surjective maps of spaces. The affine and universe hypotheses are exactly those already checked.

source.place: Paragraph preceding (4.1); Bhatt-Scholze paragraph preceding Lemma 4.2.13

proof.text: For a finite family $(E_a\to S)_a$, the space $|T|\times_S(\coprod_a E_a)$ is the disjoint union of the spaces $|T|\times_S E_a$. The inverse-image structure sheaf restricts on its $a$-th open-and-closed component to the inverse-image structure sheaf defining $V(E_a)$. Consequently the ringed spaces, hence the schemes and their inclusion maps, identify as $V(\coprod_a E_a)=\coprod_a V(E_a)$. This includes the empty family, for which both sides are the empty scheme. Together with step 8 it proves all the preservation assertions.

source.place: Locally ringed-space description following Lemma 2.2.8, applied to finite disjoint unions

proof.text: For an absolute profinite space $K$, the test scheme $T[K]$ is the inverse limit of the finite disjoint unions $\coprod_{K_j}T$ for finite quotients $K_j$ of $K$, by [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-test-object-functor]. Apply the universal-property calculation in steps 5-6 to the profinite limit $S\times K=\varprojlim_j(S\times K_j)$ over $S$. Here $V(S\times K_j)=\coprod_{K_j}T$ by the finite description in step 4. Thus it gives a canonical isomorphism $V(S\times K)\cong T[K]$. On maps $K\to L$ this isomorphism commutes with precomposition on the continuous-map coordinate of step 5, so it is natural, independently of the finite quotients used.

source.place: Factorization sentence immediately after (4.1); absolute point test objects in Section 3; Bhatt-Scholze Lemma 2.2.8

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-slice-subtopos-site-presentation] to the profinite site and its object $S$. Its localized site is exactly the site of profinite spaces over $S$ with the stated finite jointly surjective coverings. It gives $(q_{S,*}H)(K)=H(S\times K\to S)$. On the other hand [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-point-pullback] defines $p_T$ as the composite of the structure-morphism inverse image with the absolute point inverse image. The set-sheaf direct image in [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image] is evaluation on base change. Together with the definition of the test objects [def-sfb-profinite-test-objects], this gives $(p_{T,*}G)(K)=G(T[K])$: first evaluate the structure-morphism direct image at $\operatorname{Spec}\operatorname{LC}(K,\mathbf Z)$ and then use $T\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}\operatorname{Spec}\operatorname{LC}(K,\mathbf Z)=T[K]$. This computation is on sheaves of sets throughout.

source.place: Factorization after (4.1); Stacks sites.tex Tag 03CE, lemma-localize-given-products; absolute-point and scheme-base-change direct-image definitions

proof.text: For every sheaf of sets $G$ on $T_{\mathrm{proet}}$ and every profinite $K$, the direct image along the relative test functor gives $(q_{S,*}\pi_{T,*}G)(K)=G(V(S\times K))\cong G(T[K])=(p_{T,*}G)(K)$. The isomorphism is natural in $K$ by step 10 and in $G$ by evaluation. Thus the two direct-image functors are naturally isomorphic. By the composition and mate conventions of [def-trf-geometric-morphism], its adjoint mate identifies the inverse images and gives the claimed geometric-morphism isomorphism $p_T\cong q_S\pi_T$.

source.place: Factorization sentence following equation (4.1), verified on direct images

proof_origin.place: Paragraph preceding and sentence following equation (4.1), using Bhatt-Scholze Lemma 2.2.8 and its more precise ringed-space formulation; compatible-partition and universal-property details written out.
